rules.sentence: Ulnar neuropathy constitutes a common upper-extremity compression neuropathy with multiple potential entrapment sites along the nerve’s course.

The elbow, particularly the cubital tunnel, accounts for most cases of ulnar neuropathy, although clinically significant compression may also occur at the wrist within the Guyon canal, as well as in the forearm or upper arm.

Participants will gain an understanding of ulnar neuropathy's clinical manifestations, including paresthesias of the fourth and fifth digits, hand weakness, impaired grip and pinch strength, and, in advanced disease, intrinsic muscle atrophy, as well as the diagnostic processes that rely on a focused clinical evaluation supported by electrodiagnostic studies and imaging when structural causes are suspected, the management strategies, and the complications including persistent sensory loss, motor deficits, or progressive deformity.

This activity for healthcare professionals is designed to enhance the learner's competence in identifying ulnar neuropathy, performing the recommended evaluation, and implementing an appropriate interprofessional approach when managing this condition, ultimately improving clinical outcomes and reducing morbidity.

Objectives: Identify the clinical features of ulnar neuropathy.Select appropriate testing modalities to evaluate suspected ulnar neuropathy.Apply evidence-based, individualized approaches for managing ulnar neuropathy.Collaborate with the interprofessional team to manage patients with ulnar neuropathy to improve functional outcomes.
